title: Ramified base change along a Cohen coefficient extension
statement: Let $p$ be prime, let $A$ be a Cohen ring [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] with perfect residue field $k=A/pA$ (bijective Frobenius), and let $W$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Fix a uniformizer $\pi\in W$ and a local ring map $a:A\to W$ inducing an isomorphism $k\xrightarrow{\sim}W/\pi W$. Let $B$ be a Cohen ring and let $b:A\to B$ be a local ring map; write $L=B/pB$, so its residue map specifies a field inclusion $k\to L$. Form the ordinary algebra tensor product $T=W\otimes_A B$ with product $(w\otimes z)(w'\otimes z')=ww'\otimes zz'$ [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Then $T$ is a complete discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, $W\to T$, $w\mapsto w\otimes1$, is injective, local and flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $\pi\otimes1$ is a uniformizer, and $T/(\pi\otimes1)T\cong L$ by $w\otimes z\mapsto\bar w\bar z$, where $\bar w\in k\subset L$ and $\bar z\in L$.

source.place: Exposé IV 4.3.5, printed p.60, V=W′_0 tensor over W(k′_0) I(k′); complete DVR assertion underlying 4.2.5, printed p.59. Ordinary tensor is complete because W is finite free over its perfect-residue Cohen subring.

proof.text: The Cohen rings $A,B$ and the DVR $W$ are local PIDs. By [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] they are Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] applies to each. Since $p$ is nonzero in $W$ and the map $a$ is local, write $p=u\pi^e$ in $W$, with $u$ a unit and $e\ge1$. In particular $p^nW=\pi^{en}W$ and $\bigcap_n p^nW=0$, the latter following from the assumed $\pi$-adic completeness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Both $a$ and $b$ are injective: a nonzero element of $A$ is $vp^r$ with $v$ a unit; its image is nonzero in the domains $W$ and $B$ because $p$ is nonzero there. We use the given residue isomorphism to identify $W/\pi W$ with $k=A/pA$.

source.place: Tags 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr) and 0317 (definition-complete); apply the DVR element decomposition and the definition of separatedness

proof.text: The classes of $1,\pi,\ldots,\pi^{e-1}$ form a $k$-basis of $W/pW=W/\pi^eW$. For spanning, for any $w$ choose $a_0\in A$ with residue $w\bmod\pi$, write $w-a(a_0)=\pi w_1$, and repeat this operation $e$ times. For independence, lift the coefficients of a nonzero $k$-linear combination to $A$, and take its least index $j$ having nonzero residue. Coefficients of smaller index map into $pW=\pi^eW$. Modulo $\pi^eW$ the sum is therefore $\pi^j(a(a_j)+\pi z)$, with $a(a_j)+\pi z$ a unit. It cannot lie in $\pi^eW$: cancellation would put that unit in $\pi W$, since $j<e$.

source.place: Tag 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring), verification of its finite-reduction hypothesis by successive residue subtraction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] with ring $A$, ideal $pA$, module $W$ and the chosen lifts $1,\pi,\ldots,\pi^{e-1}$. Its hypotheses are: completeness of $A$ from its Cohen-ring hypothesis, $\bigcap_n p^nW=0$ from Step 1, and finite generation of $W/pW$ from Step 2. The strengthened conclusion about any lifts of generators shows that these very powers generate $W$ over $A$. They are independent as well. In a relation $\sum_{i<e}a(a_i)\pi^i=0$, Step 2 implies $a_i\in pA$ for every $i$. Divide the coefficients by $p$ and cancel the nonzero $p$ in $W$; repetition gives $a_i\in\bigcap_n p^nA=0$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Thus the displayed powers are an $A$-basis of $W$.

source.place: Tag 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring), including its proof for the specified generators; Tag 0317 (definition-complete) for separation

proof.text: Write $\pi^e=\sum_{i<e}a(c_i)\pi^i$ in that basis and put $P(X)=X^e-\sum_{i<e}c_iX^i\in A[X]$. Step 2 gives $c_i\in pA$. Write $c_i=pd_i$. In $W$ the relation gives $a(c_0)=\pi^e(1-u\sum_{1\le i<e}a(d_i)\pi^i)$; the parenthesis is a unit, since it is $1$ modulo $\pi$. If $c_0\in p^2A$, this would put $\pi^e$ in $\pi^{2e}W\subseteq\pi^{e+1}W$, a contradiction by cancellation. Hence $P$ is monic with all lower coefficients in $pA$ and constant coefficient outside $p^2A$. Evaluation induces $A[X]/(P)\to W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] its source has basis $1,X,\ldots,X^{e-1}$; the map takes this basis to the basis of Step 3, so it is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09ER (lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified), proof, polynomial presentation; coefficient argument expanded here

proof.text: Let $P_B$ be obtained by applying $b$ to the coefficients and put $Q=B[X]/(P_B)$, with $x$ the class of $X$. The presentation of Step 4 gives a map $W\to Q$ sending $\pi$ to $x$, compatible with the coefficient map $B\to Q$. The tensor universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives $T\to Q$, $w\otimes z\mapsto w(x)z$. Conversely evaluation $X\mapsto\pi\otimes1$ defines $Q\to T$, since $P_B(\pi\otimes1)=0$. These maps are inverse: on $Q$ their composite fixes $B$ and $x$, which generate $Q$; on $T$ it fixes every pure tensor, by the presentation of $W$. Thus $T\cong Q$ as $B$-algebras, with $\pi\otimes1$ corresponding to $x$. Since $c_0=pd_0\notin p^2A$, $d_0$ is a unit of $A$, so $b(c_0)=pb(d_0)\notin p^2B$. Every other lower coefficient still lies in $pB$. Apply [lem-sfb-eisenstein-quotient-dvr] to the DVR $B$, uniformizer $p$, degree $e\ge1$, and polynomial $P_B$. It yields that $Q$, hence $T$, is a DVR with maximal ideal generated by $x$.

source.place: Tag 09ER (lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified), proof, Eisenstein presentation after scalar extension

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $Q$ has $B$-basis $1,x,\ldots,x^{e-1}$. In the $A$-basis of Step 3 and this $B$-basis, $W\to Q$ takes the coefficient vector $(a_i)_{i<e}$ to $(b(a_i))_{i<e}$. It is injective by the injectivity of $b$ in Step 1. The residue map $Q\to B/pB=L$ sends $x$ to $0$ and each coefficient to its residue. Indeed quotienting by $x$ leaves $B/(b(c_0))=B/pB$, because $b(c_0)$ is $p$ times a unit. For $w=\sum_{i<e}a(a_i)\pi^i$, the image of $w\otimes z$ is $\overline{b(a_0)}\bar z=\bar w\bar z$, the required formula. Its restriction to $W$ has kernel $\pi W$ because $k\to L$ is a field inclusion. Thus $W\to T$ is local. The injective map $W\to T$ gives characteristic zero, and the computed residue field has characteristic $p$.

source.place: Tag 09ER (lemma-weakly-unramified-goes-up-along-totally-ramified), proof, explicit basis and residue identifications

proof.text: The same basis identifies $Q/p^nQ$ with $(B/p^nB)^e$ compatibly for all $n$. A compatible sequence therefore consists of $e$ compatible coefficient sequences, each lifted uniquely to $B$ by its Cohen-ring completeness. Their finite linear combination in the basis gives the unique lift to $Q$. Thus $Q$ is $p$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. The identity $p=u\pi^e$ in $W$ gives $pQ=x^eQ$, since the image of $u$ remains a unit; hence $p^nQ=x^{en}Q$. These powers are cofinal among the powers of $x$. Explicitly, from compatible residues modulo $x^m$ take the subsequence $m=en$, lift uniquely by $p$-completeness, and for each $m$ reduce an equality modulo $x^{en}$ with $en\ge m$ to recover that residue. Uniqueness follows from the same subsequence. Consequently $Q$ and $T$ are complete for their maximal ideals.

source.place: Tag 0317 (definition-complete); finite coordinate calculation and cofinal subsequence argument written out

proof.text: Finally $T$ is torsion free as a $W$-module: if $0\ne w\in W$ and $wt=0$ in $T$, its image is nonzero by Step 6, so $t=0$ because $T$ is a domain by Step 5. Since $W$ is a PID, [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] makes $T$ flat over $W$. By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] this is precisely flatness of the map $w\mapsto w\otimes1$. Together with Steps 5--7 this proves every assertion for the ordinary algebra tensor product.

S2 (elementary) shows 1..π^{e-1} is a k-basis of W/π^eW, with the independence argument at the least nonzero index. S3 meets all three hypotheses of the finite-over-complete node and proves independence by dividing by p repeatedly. S4: I recomputed a(c_0)=π^e(1-uΣ_{i>=1}a(d_i)π^i), so c_0∉p²A and A[X]/(P)≅W. S5 builds T≅Q with both maps well defined and both composites the identity; the Eisenstein hypotheses (coefficients in pB, constant term p times a unit, e>=1) are checked. S6 computes the residue B/(b(c_0))=L by w⊗z↦w̄z̄, and shows W→T is injective and local. S7 proves completeness through the basis and p^nQ=x^{en}Q. S8 gets flatness from torsion-freeness over a PID. Edge cases e=1, W=A, b=id and L imperfect or infinite over k all hold. Unused perfectness of k is kept, which matches the source.
